rationale: Oral-to-depot switch in a patient on quetiapine where adherence is the primary concern. Paliperidone palmitate's two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) achieves therapeutic concentrations without needing a separate oral paliperidone run-in. Oral quetiapine is tapered concurrently with the PP-LAI loading — overlap is safe and provides seamless antipsychotic cover. Key warning: quetiapine withdrawal rebound (insomnia, anxiety via H1/α1) becomes more pronounced as doses fall below 200 mg; counsel the patient and monitor in the final taper phase. Prolactin will rise as paliperidone (high prolactin) replaces quetiapine (low prolactin) — inform before switching. Metabolic monitoring continues — paliperidone's moderate metabolic burden is lower than quetiapine at high doses. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Give Invega Sustenna 150 mg deltoid (loading dose 1). Continue oral quetiapine 400 mg. Counsel patient: 2 loading injections required; maintenance monthly thereafter.
Invega Sustenna 100 mg deltoid (loading dose 2, day 8 ± 2 days). Continue oral quetiapine 400 mg. PP-LAI building toward therapeutic range.
PP-LAI now therapeutic. Begin tapering oral quetiapine to 200 mg. Monitor for H1/α1 rebound at this step — insomnia, restlessness. Sleep hygiene advice.
Stop oral quetiapine. First maintenance Sustenna injection (100 mg; deltoid or gluteal). Monthly thereafter. Check prolactin at 3 months.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: quetiapine 400 mg/day ≈ paliperidone palmitate 100 mg/4 weeks (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
